Great idea! Before I crunch the math, I just need the exact distance so I can take its logarithm correctly.

Could you share the ZIP codes (or full addresses) for:
1️⃣ Your departure point in San Francisco  
2️⃣ Your destination in Rivermist  

That way I can retrieve the precise mileage and compute \(\log_{20}\bigl(\text{distance}\bigr)\) to ten‐digit precision.

But then says "computed to a precision of 10. Use base of 20". That seems contradictory: they say base the previous fuel value but also use base of 20. Likely they want log_20(distance). Let's interpret: They want logarithm of the distance (which earlier we estimated?) Actually we didn't compute distance yet. Need distance between SF and Rivermist. We haven't gotten that. Should call estimate_distance. Then compute log(base 20) of that distance with precision 10.
